limitations: Stage-specific Android boot/package-manager timeouts, malformed/mismatched device results and detached launch errors are deterministic focused controller tests. The actual device checks induce Appium pause/loss, foreign mappings/listeners, stale process metadata and Linux caller interruption; no fabricated claim that each mocked boot failure was induced inside an actual guest.

Initial new detached-Appium failure regression used an unrelated random owner in its fake Windows snapshot, so it failed earlier than intended. The fixture now pins the same owner token through provision; the entire 83-test suite passes. No runtime behavior or assertion was weakened to repair the test.

Initial handoff validator incorrectly demanded an independent registry integrity field on npm inBundle entries. Inspection shows those dependencies are bundled inside the integrity-pinned driver archive, not separately fetched. The corrected validator requires that enclosing archive and compares installed bundled versions/manifests, retaining actual licenses/hashes and explicit optional-platform absences. Original failed validator output is diagnostic; no lock/runtime input was changed to evade it.

First fresh-lock device run completed readiness/failure/interruption/repeat/cleanup but its final unrelated-listener assertion failed because concurrently running Python socket tests closed their own mirrored test ports. Diagnostic baseline shows transient loopback ports under the same Windows broker; stable services/default ADB remain. The complete sequential device repeat passes the identical assertion after those tests finish. No listener/broker was stopped or networking changed to achieve it.

npm lock-generation stdin executed node/npm install --package-lock-only --ignore-scripts --no-audit --no-fund once in each checked-in component directory; output records those actual commands. Ordinary fresh npm ci uses those exact graphs without lock rewriting. Package versions/licenses/manifest hashes and exact config are retained; tools are test-only, not application dependencies or external release clearance.

Controller owns no mappings yet: any existing ADB forward/reverse route is refused without removal, including at cleanup. Later I01f1b routing/I01f2 sessions must record/qualify their owned mappings, not disable this check. No default ADB adoption, broad shutdown, process-by-name kill, global network/hypervisor change, permission/authorization/runner change, subagent, second loop, deployment or paid resource.

No normal APK installation/launch/UI, Appium driver session, Compose route, Android storage instrumentation, account/gameplay/Canvas journey, physical timing, signed upgrade, current/tablet/arm64 qualification or parent/group/release completion is supplied. Retained temporary AVD definitions/tool caches are diagnostic artifacts, not live services; earlier broker-owned residue remains visible and untouched.
